titleEn: X Spaces: Starship flight-test debrief for subscribers
titleZh: X Spaces：面向订阅者的星舰飞行测试复盘
summaryEn: In a subscriber-only Twitter Space, Musk debriefed the first integrated orbital flight test of Starship, taking questions and explaining what SpaceX learned from the launch.
summaryZh: 在一场仅限订阅者参加的Twitter Space中，马斯克复盘了星舰首次一体化轨道飞行测试，回答问题并解释SpaceX从此次发射中了解到的情况。

segments.textEn: Hey, Irene.
segments.textZh: 嘿，艾琳。

segments.textEn: Hey, Elon.
segments.textZh: 嘿，埃隆。

segments.textEn: It's been a long time.
segments.textZh: 好久不见了。

segments.textEn: Yeah, it has. That was very exciting to be in Boca Chica. You always, you always live up to your. Your promises about exciting times with SpaceX.
segments.textZh: 是啊，确实。能在博卡奇卡真是非常激动人心。你总是，你总是兑现你的。你关于SpaceX激动人心时刻的承诺。

segments.textEn: Yes.
segments.textZh: 是的。

segments.textEn: You know, punctuality is not my strong suit, but I do it deliver in the end.
segments.textZh: 你知道，守时不是我的强项，但我最终确实会交付。

segments.textEn: Yes, you do.
segments.textZh: 是的，你会。

segments.textEn: Excitement was guaranteed and it was delivered.
segments.textZh: 激动人心是有保证的，而且也兑现了。

segments.textEn: Exactly. I mean, so, yeah, we just get right into it.
segments.textZh: 没错。我的意思是，那么，是的，我们就直接开始吧。

segments.textEn: So I think probably people have enough time to get on or hopefully. So, yeah, as basically the outcome was roughly the sort of what I expected and maybe slightly exceeding my expectations, but roughly what I expected, which was or hoped for, I should say, which is that we would get clear of the pad with minimal damage to the pad. And I'm glad to report that the pad damage is actually quite small and looks like it can be repaired quickly and that we would also get significant in flight data, particularly with respect to the pressurizing of the tanks with the propellant liquids, which is called autogenous pressurization, as opposed to say Falcon 9, which uses helium pressurization.
segments.textZh: 所以我想，大家大概已经有足够的时间加入了，或者希望如此。那么，是的，基本上，结果大致就是我所预期的那种情况，也许还略微超出了我的预期，但大体符合我的预期，或者我应该说，是我所希望的，也就是我们能够离开发射台，同时对发射台造成的损伤很小。我很高兴地报告，发射台的损伤实际上相当小，看起来可以很快修复，而且我们也能够获得大量飞行数据，尤其是有关使用液体推进剂对储箱加压的数据，这叫自生增压；与之相对的是，比如猎鹰9号使用的是氦气增压。

segments.textEn: But helium is in very short supply and extremely expensive, so it's way better to essentially pressurize with the liquid form of the oxidized raw fuel. So that actually looked quite good. And we also went supersonic, so that was no problem at all.
segments.textZh: 但氦气极其短缺，而且极其昂贵，所以从本质上说，使用氧化后的原始燃料的液态形式来增压要好得多。所以那实际上看起来相当不错。我们也进入了超音速，所以那完全没有问题。

segments.textEn: And.
segments.textZh: 而且。

segments.textEn: But the. So I'm going to throw obviously some good news items here. The vehicle structural margins appear to be better than we expected. As we can tell, the vehicle is actually doing somersaults towards the end and still staying intact.
segments.textZh: 但这个。所以我显然要在这里抛出一些好消息。飞行器的结构裕度似乎比我们预期的更好。正如我们所能看出的，飞行器实际上在接近最后时翻起了跟头，但仍然保持完整。

segments.textEn: So that's also good.
segments.textZh: 所以这也很好。

segments.textEn: And yeah, so overall I actually feel like that was a great flight. SpaceX team did excellent work, we made a lot of progress and I think from a rocket standpoint and pad standpoint, we are probably ready to launch in six to eight weeks.
segments.textZh: 而且，是的，所以总体而言，我实际上觉得那是一次很棒的飞行。SpaceX团队的工作非常出色，我们取得了很大进展，而且我认为，从火箭和发射台的角度来看，我们大概能在6至8周内做好发射准备。

segments.textEn: The longest lead item on that is probably requalification of the flight termination system, because we did initiate the flight termination system, but it was not enough to. It took way too long to rupture the tanks.
segments.textZh: 其中交付周期最长的事项可能是飞行终止系统的重新认证，因为我们确实启动了飞行终止系统，但这不足以。它花了太长时间才使储箱破裂。

segments.textEn: So we need a. Basically a much. We need more detonation cord to lines up the tanks at altitude and ensure that basically the rocket explodes immediately if there's a.
segments.textZh: 所以我们需要一个。基本上是一个更……我们需要更多导爆索，以便在高空沿储箱排成线，并确保基本上在出现一个……时火箭会立即爆炸。

segments.textEn: If flight termination is necessary. So requalification of the. I'm just guessing here that requalification of the much longer detonation cord to ends up the rocket in a bad situation is probably the long lead item.
segments.textZh: 如果有必要终止飞行的话。所以，重新认证这个。我只是在这里猜测，重新认证长得多的导爆索，以便最终在糟糕情况下终结火箭，可能是交付周期最长的事项。

segments.textEn: What was the time lag?
segments.textZh: 时间延迟是多少？

segments.textEn: It was pretty long.
segments.textZh: 相当长。

segments.textEn: I think it was on the order of 40 seconds. Ish.
segments.textZh: 我想大约是40秒左右。差不多。

segments.textEn: So quite long.
segments.textZh: 所以相当长。

segments.textEn: Yeah, so now the rocket was in a relatively low air density, so the aerodynamic forces that it was experiencing would be less than if it was at a lower, you know, lower down in the atmosphere. And so the aerodynamic forces would have, I think, at a lower point in the atmosphere, aided in the destruction of the vehicle. And in fact, that's, that's kind of what, what happened. When the vehicle got to a low enough altitude, the atmospheric density was enough to cause structural failure.
segments.textZh: 是的，所以当时火箭所处位置的空气密度相对较低，因此它承受的气动力会小于它处在更低处，你知道，大气层中更低位置时的气动力。所以我认为，如果在大气层中更低的位置，气动力会有助于摧毁飞行器。而事实上，那就是，那差不多就是所发生的事情。当飞行器下降到足够低的高度时，大气密度已经足以导致结构失效。

segments.textEn: But I mean, this is obviously something that we, we want to make super sure is solid before proceeding with the next flight.
segments.textZh: 但我的意思是，这显然是我们，我们希望在进行下一次飞行之前绝对确保稳妥的事情。

segments.textEn: Let's see, I'll go through a bunch of notables. So we, we actually, at Luftorf, there were three engines that we didn't. We chose not to start, essentially, or that hit, hit aborts that. And so we actually lifted off with 30 engines, which is the minimum number of engines.
segments.textZh: 让我看看，我会逐一讲很多值得注意的事项。所以我们，我们实际上，在卢夫托夫，有3台发动机是我们没有。我们基本上选择不启动，或者它们触发了中止条件，而。所以我们实际上是用30台发动机起飞的，这是发动机的最低数量。

segments.textEn: Those engines did not explode, but they were just because the system didn't think they were healthy enough to bring them to full thrust. So they were shut down.
segments.textZh: 那些发动机没有爆炸，但它们只是因为系统认为它们的健康状况不足以让它们达到全推力。所以它们被关闭了。

segments.textEn: Then at T +27 seconds, Engine 19 lost communications concurrent with some kind of energetic event that liberated the outer heat shield from the engines 17, 18, 19 and 20 area. You can see this on video, actually. And by the way, if people have like, basically think that maybe something different from this occurred, that'd be interesting to. Because I know some people have looked very closely frame by frame at video, but this is the SpaceX best assessment after a week.
segments.textZh: 然后在 T +27 秒时，19 号发动机失去通信，与此同时发生了某种高能事件，使 17、18、19 和 20 号发动机区域的外部隔热罩脱落。实际上，你可以在视频中看到这一点。顺便说一句，如果有人基本上认为发生的事情可能与此不同，那也会很有意思。因为我知道有些人逐帧非常仔细地看过视频，但这是 SpaceX 在一周后作出的最佳评估。

segments.textEn: Anyway, so something bad happened at T +27 seconds because Engine 19 lost all communications and some kind of explosion happened to knock out the heat shields of engines 17, 18, 19 and 20.
segments.textZh: 总之，在 T +27 秒时发生了糟糕的事情，因为 19 号发动机失去了所有通信，而且发生了某种爆炸，炸掉了 17、18、19 和 20 号发动机的隔热罩。

segments.textEn: And yeah, so. And the visible fire seen from the aftan starting after this event and continuing through flight.
segments.textZh: 然后，是的，所以。而这次事件发生后，从阿夫坦看到的明显火焰开始出现，并在整个飞行过程中持续存在。

segments.textEn: The rocket kept going, though, for at T +62 seconds. We see additional aft heat shield damage near engine 30. However, the engine continues to run. And then at T85 seconds is where things really hit the fan. We see Engine 6 with loss of communication to thrust vector control. And roughly from this point onwards, we lose thrust vector control of the rocket. So we lose steering at T plus 85 seconds.
segments.textZh: 不过，火箭继续飞行，在 T +62 秒时。我们看到 30 号发动机附近的后部隔热罩出现了更多损坏。然而，发动机继续运行。然后到了 T85 秒，事情才真正变得一团糟。我们看到 6 号发动机与推力矢量控制系统失去通信。从大约这一刻起，我们失去了对火箭的推力矢量控制。所以我们在 T +85 秒时失去了转向能力。

segments.textEn: And was that engine six that kept trying to relight too?
segments.textZh: 那也是一直试图重新点火的 6 号发动机吗？

segments.textEn: Possibly. I don't know.
segments.textZh: 有可能。我不知道。

segments.textEn: Was there one? One looked like in footage, like it just kept attempting to relight, Relight, relight over and over, which is pretty wild to see. I don't think I've ever seen that before. And it was one of the center Ish engines.
segments.textZh: 有这样一台吗？画面中有一台看起来就像一直在尝试重新点火，重新点火，反复重新点火，看起来相当不可思议。我觉得自己以前从未见过这种情况。而且它是其中一台比较靠近中央的发动机。

segments.textEn: That's interesting. Okay, we do have relight logic in the center engines, but not in the outer engines? I believe so.
segments.textZh: 这很有意思。好吧，我们的中央发动机确实有重新点火逻辑，但外侧发动机没有？我想是这样。

segments.textEn: So basically, landing engines have relight logic. The perimeter engines don't. So that's entirely possible. Although if the engine is detecting significant issues, it should not be going into a relight cycle.
segments.textZh: 所以基本上，着陆发动机有重新点火逻辑。外围发动机没有。所以这完全有可能。不过，如果发动机检测到重大问题，它就不应该进入重新点火循环。

segments.textEn: What's your best guess as to what caused the initial engine issues? And then I guess it cascaded after that. But what do you think happened?
segments.textZh: 你对最初发动机问题的起因有什么最合理的猜测？然后我想，之后问题就级联扩散了。但你认为发生了什么？

segments.textEn: I think we don't know with certainty.
segments.textZh: 我认为我们无法确定。

segments.textEn: Obviously, the rocket stayed on the launch pad for a while, and we did generate quite the rock tornado at the base of the vehicle. And our first guess would have been that the rock tornado would have caused potentially significant damage to the engines. But at least we actually do not see obvious.
segments.textZh: 显然，火箭在发射台上停留了一段时间，而且我们确实在飞行器底部制造了相当猛烈的岩石龙卷风。我们最初会猜测，岩石龙卷风可能对发动机造成了严重损坏。但至少我们实际上没有看到明显的。

segments.textEn: We actually weirdly do not see evidence of the rock tornado actually damaging engines or heat shields in a material way. But it may have, but we have not yet seen evidence of that. So for the next flight, we certainly will be taking off faster. So for this flight, we were erred on the side of kind of babying the engines and just sort of gently sort of starting each engine one at a time. And there were quite. The engines on Booster seven were built over a long period of time.
segments.textZh: 奇怪的是，我们实际上没有看到证据表明岩石龙卷风确实对发动机或隔热罩造成了实质性损坏。但它或许造成了损坏，只是我们尚未看到相关证据。所以在下一次飞行中，我们肯定会更快起飞。因此在这次飞行中，我们犯的错误是偏向于有点小心呵护发动机，只是有点轻柔地、有点逐台启动每台发动机。而且有相当。助推器 7 上的发动机是在很长一段时间内制造的。

segments.textEn: So each engine was a little bit of a unique item. And, you know, whereas the engines on Booster nine, which is next, are much newer and more and more and consistent and really with significant reliability improvements over Booster seven. So I think we'll see a much more robust engine situation with Booster nine. The heat shield, or I should say the shields, which are both of force and heat shields around the engines for Booster 9 are much better because they weren't retrofitted for Booster 7, we kind of retrofitted heat shields, whereas Booster 9 is designed in, so they're much stouter.
segments.textZh: 所以每台发动机都有点独一无二。而且，你知道，相比之下，接下来使用的助推器 9 上的发动机要新得多，也更、更……而且一致，并且相较助推器 7 确实有显著的可靠性改进。所以我认为，我们会在助推器 9 上看到稳健得多的发动机状况。助推器 9 的隔热罩，或者我应该说发动机周围的防护罩，它们既是受力防护罩也是隔热罩，要好得多，因为它们不是为助推器 7 加装的，我们算是给助推器 7 加装了隔热罩，而助推器 9 在设计中就包含了它们，所以坚固得多。

segments.textEn: Will you be doing something with the Raptor Chill System on Booster 9 differently than what you did with 7?
segments.textZh: 你们会以不同于助推器 7 的方式处理助推器 9 上的猛禽发动机冷却系统吗？

segments.textEn: It kind of seems like that was like an expendable part of the pad, essentially, with having all of those hoses rip free. I'm guessing that's something you would like to avoid having to replace every time in the future.
segments.textZh: 所有那些软管都被扯脱后，看起来那基本上就像是发射台上的一个消耗性部件。我猜你们将来会希望避免每次都必须更换它。

segments.textEn: Yeah, over time, we're definitely. It needs to be like a rapid, rapid reflux capability, so there can't be any extendable items. Over time.
segments.textZh: 是的，随着时间推移，我们肯定会。它需要具备快速、快速回流能力，所以不能有任何可伸展物品。随着时间推移。

segments.textEn: It was actually just good, good to get this. This vehicle off the ground because we've made so many improvements in and Booster nine and beyond that.
segments.textZh: 实际上，能让这。这艘飞行器升空确实很好，很好，因为我们已经在助推器 9 以及之后的型号上做出了如此多的改进。

segments.textEn: We really just needed to fly this vehicle and then move on to the much improved Booster nine and later ship designs.
segments.textZh: 我们确实只需要让这艘飞行器飞起来，然后转向改进了许多的助推器 9 和后续飞船设计。

segments.textEn: So the thing we want to make sure of probably most with the next flight is that we do not have that any kind of central nexus that controls that affects multiple engines is extremely robust and with, you know, extra shielding so that we don't have a sort of a single point that can take out multiple engines. And for sure we don't want a single point that can take out thrust vector control, which is engine steering.
segments.textZh: 所以在下一次飞行中，我们大概最需要确保的是，我们不会有那种……任何控制、影响多台发动机的中央枢纽都极其稳健，并且，你知道，要有额外的防护，这样就不会出现某个单点导致多台发动机失效的情况。而且我们肯定不希望有一个单点能够导致推力矢量控制失效，也就是发动机转向失效。

segments.textEn: So.
segments.textZh: 所以。

segments.textEn: The range of detail we can go into here is like sort of level nine rocket wizardry all the way to how do rockets work?
segments.textZh: 我们在这里可以深入到的细节范围，大概可以从 9 级火箭巫术一直到火箭是怎么工作的？

segments.textEn: Understood.
segments.textZh: 明白了。

segments.textEn: Can I try again? I can confirm that we have all been doing a massive amount of speculation out here and I guess one of the big points that a lot of us have been wondering is related to stage separation. So I guess the two part question, like what actually triggers second stage ignition? And also the second part of that question, did ship 24 attempt to light its engines after the destruction of Booster 7?
segments.textZh: 我能再试一次吗？我可以确认，我们这里所有人一直都在进行大量猜测，我想，我们很多人一直想知道的一个重点与级间分离有关。所以我想这是个分成两部分的问题，比如究竟是什么触发第二级点火？还有这个问题的第二部分，在助推器 7 被摧毁后，飞船 24 是否曾尝试点燃其发动机？

segments.textEn: No, it did not. When flight termination is executed, it's executed on both. So the ship, the ship currently does not attempt to save itself.
segments.textZh: 没有，它没有。当执行飞行终止时，两者都会执行。所以飞船，飞船目前不会尝试自救。

segments.textEn: Arguably, maybe it should. That's a good point.
segments.textZh: 可以说，也许它应该这样做。这一点很好。

segments.textEn: Yeah, it's crazy. It looks like the engines lit after the booster let go and after the
segments.textZh: 是啊，太疯狂了。看起来发动机在助推器松脱之后、在……之后点燃了

segments.textEn: booster finally blew up.
segments.textZh: 助推器最终爆炸。

segments.textEn: Like there's what looks like engine ignition. Pretty wild.
segments.textZh: 就像那里出现了看起来像发动机点火的东西。相当不可思议。

segments.textEn: That is. That has not been reported to me in the data reviews that it's not impossible, but it's not been reported to me.
segments.textZh: 那确实是。在数据审查中没有人向我报告过这一点，它并非不可能，但没有人向我报告过。

segments.textEn: That is certainly not what the ship should be doing after a termination event. So.
segments.textZh: 这当然不是飞船在发生终止事件后应该做的事。所以。

segments.textEn: The big things that are important for the next flight are ensuring that thrust vector, we don't lose thrust vector control. Sort of isolation of thrust vector control, which with the Booster nine is a lot easier because we use electric motors to steer the engines as opposed to hydraulic actuators where you've got a common manifold between the hydraulic actuators. So if you lose hydraulic pressure, you can lose multiple engines.
segments.textZh: 对下一次飞行来说，重要的大事是确保推力矢量，确保我们不会失去推力矢量控制。也就是对推力矢量控制进行隔离，这在助推器 9 上要容易得多，因为我们使用电动机来操纵发动机，而不是使用液压作动器；液压作动器之间有一个共用歧管。所以如果液压压力丧失，你可能会失去多台发动机。

segments.textEn: Essentially if you have some kind of failure in the hydraulic system, the electric actuated engines will be much more isolated and not have like a single event failure as long as they did not lose power or comms.
segments.textZh: 基本上，如果液压系统出现某种故障，电动作动的发动机将得到好得多的隔离，只要它们没有失去电力或通信，就不会出现类似单一事件故障的情况。

segments.textEn: Elon, since you've gone ahead and excavated your launch mount a bit, I assume you're going to go ahead and put in that the steel grid and the water deluge. Do you think that that will fully address the issue of the wider than expected debris field and are you expecting any pushback from environmental and kind of community groups that this, that this event did put debris where it wasn't expected?
segments.textZh: 埃隆，既然你们已经把发射台基座挖开了一些，我想你们接下来会安装那个钢制格栅和喷水降温系统。你认为这会彻底解决碎片散布范围超出预期的问题吗？你是否预计环境和某种社区团体会因这次，这次事件把碎片散落到原本没有预料到的地方而提出任何反对？

segments.textEn: Yeah, we're going to be putting down a lot of steel I mean the debris is really just, you know, basically sand.
segments.textZh: 是的，我们会铺设大量钢材，我的意思是，那些碎片其实只是，你知道，基本上就是沙子。

segments.textEn: So it's not like, not toxic at all or anything. It's just like a sandstorm essentially. Basically a human made sandstorm. But we don't want to do that again.
segments.textZh: 所以它并不是，比如说，完全没有毒性或什么的。它基本上就像一场沙尘暴。基本上是一场人为制造的沙尘暴。但我们不想再这样做了。
